def run {S Q A X : Type*} (next : S → Sum X Q) (update : S → Q → A → S)
    (oracle : Q → A) : ℕ → S → (S × Option X) × ℕ
  | fuel, s => match next s with
    | .inl x => ((s, some x), 0)
    | .inr q => match fuel with
      | 0 => ((s, none), 0)
      | n+1 =>
        let answer := oracle q
        let tail := run next update oracle n (update s q answer)
        (tail.1, tail.2+1)

MeasurableSpace specifies a sigma algebra. Products and Sum carry their standard product and disjoint-sum sigma algebras; MeasurableSpace.comap g m is the pullback sigma algebra along g. Option has constructors none and some; its sigma algebra here is exactly the displayed pullback along none ↦ Sum.inl () and some x ↦ Sum.inr x.

Measure Ω is a measure on the displayed measurable space. IsProbabilityMeasure μ means μ has total mass one. μ.map h is the pushforward measure under h. Integrable g μ and ∫ ω, g ω ∂μ refer to Bochner integrability and the ordinary integral under precisely μ. Natural-number counts are coerced to real numbers in those integrals.

reconstruction.text:
Let S, Q, A, B, X, and Ω be arbitrary types, each with an arbitrary
specified sigma algebra (and possibly different type universes).
Products have the standard product sigma algebras and sums the standard
disjoint-sum sigma algebras. Give Option X precisely the pullback sigma
algebra under the map to Unit ⊕ X that sends none to inl(()) and some(x)
to inr(x).

For every probability measure μ on Ω, every next : S → X ⊕ Q,
update : S → Q → B → S, oracle : Q → A, target : Q → B,
decode : Q → A → B, and initial : Ω → S, assume that next is
measurable, (s,q,b) ↦ update(s,q,b) is measurable, oracle is measurable,
(q,a) ↦ decode(q,a) is measurable, and initial is measurable. Assume
also that decode(q, oracle(q)) = target(q) for every q in Q.
There is no separate measurability hypothesis on target.

Use the run recursion specified below, with the answer type instantiated
as appropriate. For every natural number N, define maps
R,T : Ω → (S × Option X) × ℕ by
  R(ω) = run(next, (s,q,a) ↦ update(s,q,decode(q,a)), oracle,
             N, initial(ω)),
  T(ω) = run(next, update, target, N, initial(ω)).
Write c_R(ω) and c_T(ω) for their outer natural-number components.
Then all the following hold together:
  1. R and T are measurable.
  2. For every ω in Ω, R(ω) = T(ω) and c_R(ω) ≤ N.
     This equality is of the entire returned record: the final state,
     the optional terminal result, and the count.
  3. The pushforward measures μ.map R and μ.map T are equal.
  4. μ.map R is a probability measure.
  5. The real-valued map ω ↦ (c_R(ω) : ℝ) is Bochner integrable under μ.
  6. ∫ (c_R(ω) : ℝ) dμ(ω) = ∫ (c_T(ω) : ℝ) dμ(ω).
  7. ∫ (c_R(ω) : ℝ) dμ(ω) ≤ (N : ℝ).
Both integrals use this same μ; the counts and N are coerced from ℕ
to ℝ for these real-valued integral assertions.

The generic run(next, update, oracle, N, s) returns ((s_final, r), c),
where r is in Option X and c is a natural number. Its exact recursion is:
first inspect next(s), even when N = 0. If next(s) = inl(x), return
((s, some(x)), 0). If next(s) = inr(q) and N = 0, return ((s, none), 0).
If next(s) = inr(q) and N = n + 1, let a = oracle(q), evaluate
run(next, update, oracle, n, update(s, q, a)) = (t, c), and return
(t, c + 1). Thus the state/result pair in a recursive return is the
tail's entire pair, and the count increases by one only in this last
branch. A terminal result can be returned at zero fuel. A none result
occurs when a query is requested with zero fuel; it is not a terminal
result value. No count is charged by either nonrecursive branch.

/-!
# Measurable adaptive oracle simulation

Author-derived probability interface for the exact oracle equivalence in
Zhou--Suzuki arXiv:2610.20492v1 Section2 Equation1. We reuse the canonical
finite-fuel interpreter without padding actual query counts. A missing output
is exhaustion, not a successful sample. This theorem does not assert source
algorithm representation or a class-uniform query-complexity bound.
-/
open MeasureTheory
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.QuadraticRegularizationOracle
set_option autoImplicit false
universe uS uQ uA uB uX uΩ

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.AdaptiveOracleSimulation

private theorem run_simulation_and_cap
    {S : Type uS} {Q : Type uQ} {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB} {X : Type uX}
    (next : S → Sum X Q) (update : S → Q → B → S)
    (oracle : Q → A) (target : Q → B) (decode : Q → A → B)
    (hdecode : ∀ q, decode q (oracle q) = target q) (fuel : ℕ) :
    ∀ s, run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel s =
      run next update target fuel s ∧
      (run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel s).2 ≤ fuel := by
  induction fuel with
  | zero =>
      intro s
      cases h : next s <;> simp [run, h]
  | succ n ih =>
      intro s
      cases h : next s with
      | inl x => simp [run, h]
      | inr q =>
          have step (upd : S → Q → B → S) (O : Q → B) :
              run next upd O (n+1) s =
                let tail := run next upd O n (upd s q (O q))
                (tail.1, tail.2+1) := by rw [run, h]
          have stepA (upd : S → Q → A → S) (O : Q → A) :
              run next upd O (n+1) s =
                let tail := run next upd O n (upd s q (O q))
                (tail.1, tail.2+1) := by rw [run, h]
          have hr := ih (update s q (target q))
          constructor
          · simpa only [stepA, step, hdecode] using
              congrArg (fun r : (S × Option X) × ℕ => (r.1, r.2+1)) hr.1
          · simpa only [stepA, hdecode] using Nat.succ_le_succ hr.2

private theorem measurable_run
    {S : Type uS} {Q : Type uQ} {A : Type uA} {X : Type uX}
    [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace Q] [MeasurableSpace A]
    [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace (Option X)]
    (next : S → Sum X Q) (update : S → Q → A → S) (oracle : Q → A)
    (hnext : Measurable next)
    (hupdate : Measurable (fun p : S × Q × A => update p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2))
    (horacle : Measurable oracle) (hsome : Measurable (@Option.some X))
    (fuel : ℕ) : Measurable (run next update oracle fuel) := by
  have hl : Measurable (fun p : S × X => ((p.1, some p.2), (0 : ℕ))) :=
    (measurable_fst.prodMk (hsome.comp measurable_snd)).prodMk measurable_const
  have hdist : Measurable (fun s : S =>
      (MeasurableEquiv.prodSumDistrib S X Q) (s, next s)) :=
    (MeasurableEquiv.prodSumDistrib S X Q).measurable.comp
      (measurable_id.prodMk hnext)
  induction fuel with
  | zero =>
      have hr : Measurable (fun p : S × Q => ((p.1, (none : Option X)), (0 : ℕ))) :=
        (measurable_fst.prodMk measurable_const).prodMk measurable_const
      convert (hl.sumElim hr).comp hdist using 1
      funext s
      cases h : next s <;> rw [run, h] <;>
        simp only [Function.comp_apply, h] <;> rfl
  | succ n ih =>
      have hstep : Measurable (fun p : S × Q => update p.1 p.2 (oracle p.2)) :=
        hupdate.comp (measurable_fst.prodMk
          (measurable_snd.prodMk (horacle.comp measurable_snd)))
      have htail := ih.comp hstep
      have hadd : Measurable (fun n : ℕ => n+1) := measurable_of_countable _
      have hr : Measurable (fun p : S × Q =>
          let tail := run next update oracle n (update p.1 p.2 (oracle p.2))
          (tail.1, tail.2+1)) :=
        (measurable_fst.comp htail).prodMk (hadd.comp (measurable_snd.comp htail))
      convert (hl.sumElim hr).comp hdist using 1
      funext s
      cases h : next s <;> rw [run, h] <;>
        simp only [Function.comp_apply, h] <;> rfl

/-- Exact reply simulation preserves the measurable seeded joint execution
law and the actual, pointwise bounded query cost and its ordinary expectation. -/
theorem measurable_simulation_joint_law_and_cost :
  ∀ {S : Type uS} {Q : Type uQ} {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB}
      {X : Type uX} {Ω : Type uΩ}
      [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace Q] [MeasurableSpace A]
      [MeasurableSpace B] [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Ω],
      letI : MeasurableSpace (Option X) := MeasurableSpace.comap
        (fun x : Option X => x.elim (Sum.inl () : Unit ⊕ X) Sum.inr) inferInstance
      ∀ (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
      (next : S → Sum X Q) (update : S → Q → B → S)
      (oracle : Q → A) (target : Q → B) (decode : Q → A → B)
      (initial : Ω → S),
      Measurable next →
      Measurable (fun p : S × Q × B => update p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) →
      Measurable oracle →
      Measurable (fun p : Q × A => decode p.1 p.2) →
      Measurable initial →
      (∀ q, decode q (oracle q) = target q) →
      ∀ fuel : ℕ,
        let baseRun : Ω → (S × Option X) × ℕ := fun ω =>
          run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel (initial ω)
        let targetRun : Ω → (S × Option X) × ℕ := fun ω =>
          run next update target fuel (initial ω)
        Measurable baseRun ∧ Measurable targetRun ∧
        (∀ ω, baseRun ω = targetRun ω ∧ (baseRun ω).2 ≤ fuel) ∧
        μ.map baseRun = μ.map targetRun ∧
        IsProbabilityMeasure (μ.map baseRun) ∧
        Integrable (fun ω => ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ)) μ ∧
        (∫ ω, ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) = (∫ ω, ((targetRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) ∧
        (∫ ω, ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) ≤ (fuel : ℝ) := by
  intro S Q A B X Ω mS mQ mA mB mX mΩ
  let : MeasurableSpace (Option X) := MeasurableSpace.comap
    (fun x : Option X => x.elim (Sum.inl () : Unit ⊕ X) Sum.inr) inferInstance
  dsimp only
  intro μ hμ next update oracle target decode initial hnext hupdate horacle hdecodeMeas
    hinitial hdecode fuel
  have hsome : Measurable (@Option.some X) := by
    apply Measurable.of_comap_le
    change MeasurableSpace.comap Option.some
      (MeasurableSpace.comap
        (fun x : Option X => x.elim (Sum.inl () : Unit ⊕ X) Sum.inr) inferInstance) ≤ _
    rw [MeasurableSpace.comap_comp]
    exact (measurable_inr : Measurable (Sum.inr : X → Unit ⊕ X)).comap_le
  let baseRun : Ω → (S × Option X) × ℕ := fun ω =>
    run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel (initial ω)
  let targetRun : Ω → (S × Option X) × ℕ := fun ω =>
    run next update target fuel (initial ω)
  have hcorrected : Measurable (fun p : S × Q × A =>
      update p.1 p.2.1 (decode p.2.1 p.2.2)) :=
    hupdate.comp (measurable_fst.prodMk
      (measurable_snd.fst.prodMk (hdecodeMeas.comp measurable_snd)))
  have hb : Measurable baseRun :=
    (measurable_run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle
      hnext hcorrected horacle hsome fuel).comp hinitial
  have he (ω : Ω) : baseRun ω = targetRun ω ∧ (baseRun ω).2 ≤ fuel :=
    run_simulation_and_cap next update oracle target decode hdecode fuel (initial ω)
  have heq : baseRun = targetRun := funext fun ω => (he ω).1
  have ht : Measurable targetRun := by rw [← heq]; exact hb
  have hlaw : μ.map baseRun = μ.map targetRun := congrArg (fun f => μ.map f) heq
  have hprob : IsProbabilityMeasure (μ.map baseRun) :=
    Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map hb.aemeasurable
  have hcount : Measurable (fun ω => ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ)) :=
    (measurable_of_countable (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ))).comp (measurable_snd.comp hb)
  have hbound (ω : Ω) : ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ≤ (fuel : ℝ) :=
    Nat.cast_le.mpr (he ω).2
  have hint : Integrable (fun ω => ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ)) μ :=
    (integrable_const (fuel : ℝ)).mono' hcount.aestronglyMeasurable
      (ae_of_all _ fun ω => by
        rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _)]
        exact hbound ω)
  have hcost : (∫ ω, ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) =
      (∫ ω, ((targetRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) :=
    integral_congr_ae (ae_of_all _ fun ω =>
      congrArg (fun r : (S × Option X) × ℕ => (r.2 : ℝ)) (he ω).1)
  have hmean : (∫ ω, ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) ≤ (fuel : ℝ) := by
    simpa using integral_mono hint (integrable_const (fuel : ℝ)) hbound
  exact ⟨hb, ht, he, hlaw, hprob, hint, hcost, hmean⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.AdaptiveOracleSimulation

The interpreter checks next even at zero fuel. An immediate halt returns some-output and count zero. An outstanding request with zero fuel returns none and count zero. Give \(\operatorname{Option}X\) exactly the pullback sigma algebra along \(\mathrm{none}\mapsto\mathrm{inl}()\), \(\mathrm{some}(x)\mapsto\mathrm{inr}(x)\); no StandardBorel hypothesis is imposed on \(X\).

The program data are \(\mathrm{next}:S\to X\sqcup Q\), \(\mathrm{update}:S\to Q\to B\to S\), an oracle \(o:Q\to A\), a target reply \(t:Q\to B\), a decoder \(\delta:Q\to A\to B\), and an initialization \(i:\Omega\to S\). Assume the displayed next, update, oracle, decoder and initialization maps measurable, and exact commutation \(\delta(q,o(q))=t(q)\) for every \(q\). No separate target-reply measurability premise is required.

For arbitrary fuel \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(R_\delta(\omega)\) runs the existing interpreter from \(i(\omega)\) with update \(\mathrm{update}(s,q,\delta(q,a))\) and oracle \(o\); \(R_t(\omega)\) uses update and target \(t\). Each result is \(((s_{\mathrm{final}},\operatorname{Option}X),C)\), including the actual number \(C\) of oracle interactions.

The interpreter checks next even at zero fuel. An immediate halt returns some-output and count zero. An outstanding request with zero fuel returns none and count zero. A funded request makes one oracle call and recurses with one less fuel. Early halts keep their smaller actual cost; none is fuel exhaustion and is never a successful sample.

The associated private application fixes \(d\ge2\), \(\kappa\ge2\), \(E=\mathbb R^d\) with its literal Borel sigma algebra, and the same Option pullback sigma algebra. The common seed law, next, updateFO, updateMV and initial state are quantified before every full orthogonal \(O\). For \(\theta_i=(i+\tfrac12)\pi/d\), \(A=O\operatorname{diag}((\kappa+1)/2+(\kappa-1)\cos\theta_i/2)O^\top\), use \(f(x)=x^\top Ax/2\), \(\mathrm{mv}(x)=Ax\), and the genuine \(\mathrm{fo}(x)=(f(x),\nabla f(x))\). Lean indices \(i=0,\ldots,d-1\) reproduce the source midpoint grid.

T compares two program-specific pairs: foViaMV with foRun under updateFO, decoding \((x,y)\mapsto(\langle x,y\rangle/2,y)\); and mvViaFO with mvRun under updateMV, projecting the gradient coordinate. It does not equate runs of unrelated update policies. Measurability of the actual oracles, the genuine gradient identity, run measurability and count integrability are established internally rather than appended as T premises.

A funded request decodes the actual answer to exactly the target answer, so both executions enter the identical updated state. Induction therefore preserves the entire terminal state/output/count tuple and bounds its actual count by fuel. This does not pad a short execution to the budget.

private theorem run_simulation_and_cap
    {S : Type uS} {Q : Type uQ} {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB} {X : Type uX}
    (next : S → Sum X Q) (update : S → Q → B → S)
    (oracle : Q → A) (target : Q → B) (decode : Q → A → B)
    (hdecode : ∀ q, decode q (oracle q) = target q) (fuel : ℕ) :
    ∀ s, run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel s =
      run next update target fuel s ∧
      (run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel s).2 ≤ fuel := by
  induction fuel with
  | zero =>
      intro s
      cases h : next s <;> simp [run, h]
  | succ n ih =>
      intro s
      cases h : next s with
      | inl x => simp [run, h]
      | inr q =>
          have step (upd : S → Q → B → S) (O : Q → B) :
              run next upd O (n+1) s =
                let tail := run next upd O n (upd s q (O q))
                (tail.1, tail.2+1) := by rw [run, h]
          have stepA (upd : S → Q → A → S) (O : Q → A) :
              run next upd O (n+1) s =
                let tail := run next upd O n (upd s q (O q))
                (tail.1, tail.2+1) := by rw [run, h]
          have hr := ih (update s q (target q))
          constructor
          · simpa only [stepA, step, hdecode] using
              congrArg (fun r : (S × Option X) × ℕ => (r.1, r.2+1)) hr.1
          · simpa only [stepA, hdecode] using Nat.succ_le_succ hr.2

private theorem measurable_run
    {S : Type uS} {Q : Type uQ} {A : Type uA} {X : Type uX}
    [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace Q] [MeasurableSpace A]
    [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace (Option X)]
    (next : S → Sum X Q) (update : S → Q → A → S) (oracle : Q → A)
    (hnext : Measurable next)
    (hupdate : Measurable (fun p : S × Q × A => update p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2))
    (horacle : Measurable oracle) (hsome : Measurable (@Option.some X))
    (fuel : ℕ) : Measurable (run next update oracle fuel) := by
  have hl : Measurable (fun p : S × X => ((p.1, some p.2), (0 : ℕ))) :=
    (measurable_fst.prodMk (hsome.comp measurable_snd)).prodMk measurable_const
  have hdist : Measurable (fun s : S =>
      (MeasurableEquiv.prodSumDistrib S X Q) (s, next s)) :=
    (MeasurableEquiv.prodSumDistrib S X Q).measurable.comp
      (measurable_id.prodMk hnext)
  induction fuel with
  | zero =>
      have hr : Measurable (fun p : S × Q => ((p.1, (none : Option X)), (0 : ℕ))) :=
        (measurable_fst.prodMk measurable_const).prodMk measurable_const
      convert (hl.sumElim hr).comp hdist using 1
      funext s
      cases h : next s <;> rw [run, h] <;>
        simp only [Function.comp_apply, h] <;> rfl
  | succ n ih =>
      have hstep : Measurable (fun p : S × Q => update p.1 p.2 (oracle p.2)) :=
        hupdate.comp (measurable_fst.prodMk
          (measurable_snd.prodMk (horacle.comp measurable_snd)))
      have htail := ih.comp hstep
      have hadd : Measurable (fun n : ℕ => n+1) := measurable_of_countable _
      have hr : Measurable (fun p : S × Q =>
          let tail := run next update oracle n (update p.1 p.2 (oracle p.2))
          (tail.1, tail.2+1)) :=
        (measurable_fst.comp htail).prodMk (hadd.comp (measurable_snd.comp htail))
      convert (hl.sumElim hr).comp hdist using 1
      funext s
      cases h : next s <;> rw [run, h] <;>
        simp only [Function.comp_apply, h] <;> rfl

theorem measurable_simulation_joint_law_and_cost :
  ∀ {S : Type uS} {Q : Type uQ} {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB}
      {X : Type uX} {Ω : Type uΩ}
      [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace Q] [MeasurableSpace A]
      [MeasurableSpace B] [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Ω],
      letI : MeasurableSpace (Option X) := MeasurableSpace.comap
        (fun x : Option X => x.elim (Sum.inl () : Unit ⊕ X) Sum.inr) inferInstance
      ∀ (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
      (next : S → Sum X Q) (update : S → Q → B → S)
      (oracle : Q → A) (target : Q → B) (decode : Q → A → B)
      (initial : Ω → S),
      Measurable next →
      Measurable (fun p : S × Q × B => update p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) →
      Measurable oracle →
      Measurable (fun p : Q × A => decode p.1 p.2) →
      Measurable initial →
      (∀ q, decode q (oracle q) = target q) →
      ∀ fuel : ℕ,
        let baseRun : Ω → (S × Option X) × ℕ := fun ω =>
          run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel (initial ω)
        let targetRun : Ω → (S × Option X) × ℕ := fun ω =>
          run next update target fuel (initial ω)
        Measurable baseRun ∧ Measurable targetRun ∧
        (∀ ω, baseRun ω = targetRun ω ∧ (baseRun ω).2 ≤ fuel) ∧
        μ.map baseRun = μ.map targetRun ∧
        IsProbabilityMeasure (μ.map baseRun) ∧
        Integrable (fun ω => ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ)) μ ∧
        (∫ ω, ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) = (∫ ω, ((targetRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) ∧
        (∫ ω, ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) ≤ (fuel : ℝ) := by
  intro S Q A B X Ω mS mQ mA mB mX mΩ
  let : MeasurableSpace (Option X) := MeasurableSpace.comap
    (fun x : Option X => x.elim (Sum.inl () : Unit ⊕ X) Sum.inr) inferInstance
  dsimp only
  intro μ hμ next update oracle target decode initial hnext hupdate horacle hdecodeMeas
    hinitial hdecode fuel
  have hsome : Measurable (@Option.some X) := by
    apply Measurable.of_comap_le
    change MeasurableSpace.comap Option.some
      (MeasurableSpace.comap
        (fun x : Option X => x.elim (Sum.inl () : Unit ⊕ X) Sum.inr) inferInstance) ≤ _
    rw [MeasurableSpace.comap_comp]
    exact (measurable_inr : Measurable (Sum.inr : X → Unit ⊕ X)).comap_le

def run {S Q A X : Type*} (next : S → Sum X Q) (update : S → Q → A → S)
    (oracle : Q → A) : ℕ → S → (S × Option X) × ℕ
  | fuel, s => match next s with
    | .inl x => ((s, some x), 0)
    | .inr q => match fuel with
      | 0 => ((s, none), 0)
      | n+1 =>
        let answer := oracle q
        let tail := run next update oracle n (update s q answer)
        (tail.1, tail.2+1)

MeasurableSpace specifies a sigma algebra. Products and Sum carry their standard product and disjoint-sum sigma algebras; MeasurableSpace.comap g m is the pullback sigma algebra along g. Option has constructors none and some; its sigma algebra here is exactly the displayed pullback along none ↦ Sum.inl () and some x ↦ Sum.inr x.

Measure Ω is a measure on the displayed measurable space. IsProbabilityMeasure μ means μ has total mass one. μ.map h is the pushforward measure under h. Integrable g μ and ∫ ω, g ω ∂μ refer to Bochner integrability and the ordinary integral under precisely μ. Natural-number counts are coerced to real numbers in those integrals.

EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) is the finite-dimensional real Euclidean space with its displayed Borel sigma algebra. WithLp.ofLp and WithLp.toLp 2 identify its coordinates with Fin d → ℝ. A *ᵥ x is matrix-vector multiplication, x ⬝ᵥ y is the coordinate dot product, inner ℝ x y is the Euclidean inner product, and Matrix.orthogonalGroup is the full real orthogonal group.

The standard definition of gradient is: gradient (f : F → 𝕜) (x : F) := (toDual 𝕜 F).symm (fderiv 𝕜 f x). Here fderiv is the totalized Fréchet derivative and toDual is the Riesz correspondence. This definition supplies no derivative formula for the particular f in the statement.

For every natural number d with 2 ≤ d, and then every real number κ
with 2 ≤ κ, let E = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), equipped with its Borel
sigma algebra. Identify its coordinates with Fin d → ℝ by
WithLp.ofLp and WithLp.toLp 2. Give Option E precisely the pullback
sigma algebra under none ↦ inl(()) and some(x) ↦ inr(x) into Unit ⊕ E.
Products and sums have their standard product and disjoint-sum sigma
algebras.

For every type S and type Ω, each with an arbitrary specified sigma
algebra, every probability measure μ on Ω, every
  next : S → E ⊕ E,
  updateFO : S → E → (ℝ × E) → S,
  updateMV : S → E → E → S,
  initial : Ω → S,
assume next is measurable, (s,x,a) ↦ updateFO(s,x,a) is measurable,
(s,x,y) ↦ updateMV(s,x,y) is measurable, and initial is measurable.
Here the left E in E ⊕ E is the terminal-result type and the right E
is the query type. The two update functions are arbitrary; no relation
between them is assumed.

For every natural number N and then every O in the full real
orthogonal group on Fin d, define, for each i in Fin d,
  θ_i = ((i.val : ℝ) + 1/2) · π / (d : ℝ),
  λ_i = (κ + 1)/2 + ((κ - 1)/2) · cos(θ_i),
  A = O · diagonal(i ↦ λ_i) · Oᵀ.
Matrix indices are Fin d, whose index values are 0,...,d−1.
For x in E, let x̄ = WithLp.ofLp x and define
  f(x) = (x̄ · (A x̄))/2,
  mv(x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (A x̄),
  fo(x) = (f(x), gradient f(x)).
The dot here is the coordinate dot product; the matrix products and
transpose are exactly the displayed real matrix operations. The
gradient is the Riesz inverse of the totalized Fréchet derivative,
gradient f(x) = (toDual ℝ E)⁻¹(fderiv ℝ f x). Its definition does not
replace it in this theorem by an asserted coordinate formula.

Use the run recursion specified below, with terminal type and query
type both E and with the appropriate answer type. Define four maps
Ω → (S × Option E) × ℕ by
  F(ω) = run(next, updateFO, fo, N, initial(ω)),
  F_M(ω) = run(next,
              (s,x,y) ↦ updateFO(s,x,(⟨x,y⟩/2,y)),
              mv, N, initial(ω)),
  M(ω) = run(next, updateMV, mv, N, initial(ω)),
  M_F(ω) = run(next,
              (s,x,(r,y)) ↦ updateMV(s,x,y),
              fo, N, initial(ω)).
The inner product ⟨x,y⟩ in F_M is the real Euclidean inner product.
Let c_H denote the outer natural-number component of any one of these
returned maps H.

All the following assertions hold together. First, for the pair
(F_M,F): F_M and F are measurable; for every ω in Ω,
F_M(ω) = F(ω) and c_{F_M}(ω) ≤ N; μ.map F_M = μ.map F;
μ.map F_M is a probability measure; ω ↦ (c_{F_M}(ω) : ℝ) is Bochner
integrable under μ;
  ∫ (c_{F_M}(ω) : ℝ) dμ(ω) = ∫ (c_F(ω) : ℝ) dμ(ω);
and
  ∫ (c_{F_M}(ω) : ℝ) dμ(ω) ≤ (N : ℝ).
Second, for the pair (M_F,M): M_F and M are measurable; for every
ω in Ω, M_F(ω) = M(ω) and c_{M_F}(ω) ≤ N;
μ.map M_F = μ.map M; μ.map M_F is a probability measure;
ω ↦ (c_{M_F}(ω) : ℝ) is Bochner integrable under μ;
  ∫ (c_{M_F}(ω) : ℝ) dμ(ω) = ∫ (c_M(ω) : ℝ) dμ(ω);
and
  ∫ (c_{M_F}(ω) : ℝ) dμ(ω) ≤ (N : ℝ).
Each pointwise equality is equality of the entire final state,
optional terminal result, and natural-number count, for every ω,
not merely almost everywhere. All integrals are under the one
displayed μ, with natural-number counts and N coerced to ℝ.

The generic run(next, update, oracle, N, s) returns ((s_final, r), c),
where r is in Option E and c is a natural number. Its exact recursion is:
first inspect next(s), even when N = 0. If next(s) = inl(x), return
((s, some(x)), 0). If next(s) = inr(q) and N = 0, return ((s, none), 0).
If next(s) = inr(q) and N = n + 1, let a = oracle(q), evaluate
run(next, update, oracle, n, update(s, q, a)) = (t, c), and return
(t, c + 1). Thus the state/result pair in a recursive return is the
tail's entire pair, and the count increases by one only in this last
branch. A terminal result can be returned at zero fuel. A none result
occurs when a query is requested with zero fuel; it is not a terminal
result value. No count is charged by either nonrecursive branch.

private theorem run_simulation_and_cap
    {S : Type uS} {Q : Type uQ} {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB} {X : Type uX}
    (next : S → Sum X Q) (update : S → Q → B → S)
    (oracle : Q → A) (target : Q → B) (decode : Q → A → B)
    (hdecode : ∀ q, decode q (oracle q) = target q) (fuel : ℕ) :
    ∀ s, run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel s =
      run next update target fuel s ∧
      (run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel s).2 ≤ fuel := by
  induction fuel with
  | zero =>
      intro s
      cases h : next s <;> simp [run, h]
  | succ n ih =>
      intro s
      cases h : next s with
      | inl x => simp [run, h]
      | inr q =>
          have step (upd : S → Q → B → S) (O : Q → B) :
              run next upd O (n+1) s =
                let tail := run next upd O n (upd s q (O q))
                (tail.1, tail.2+1) := by rw [run, h]
          have stepA (upd : S → Q → A → S) (O : Q → A) :
              run next upd O (n+1) s =
                let tail := run next upd O n (upd s q (O q))
                (tail.1, tail.2+1) := by rw [run, h]
          have hr := ih (update s q (target q))
          constructor
          · simpa only [stepA, step, hdecode] using
              congrArg (fun r : (S × Option X) × ℕ => (r.1, r.2+1)) hr.1
          · simpa only [stepA, hdecode] using Nat.succ_le_succ hr.2

private theorem measurable_run

    (horacle : Measurable oracle) (hsome : Measurable (@Option.some X))

  have hdist : Measurable (fun s : S =>

    (MeasurableEquiv.prodSumDistrib S X Q).measurable.comp
      (measurable_id.prodMk hnext)
  induction fuel with
  | zero =>

      funext s
      cases h : next s <;> rw [run, h] <;>
        simp only [Function.comp_apply, h] <;> rfl
  | succ n ih =>
      have hstep : Measurable (fun p : S × Q => update p.1 p.2 (oracle p.2)) :=

          (measurable_snd.prodMk (horacle.comp measurable_snd)))
      have htail := ih.comp hstep
      have hadd : Measurable (fun n : ℕ => n+1) := measurable_of_countable _
      have hr : Measurable (fun p : S × Q =>
          let tail := run next update oracle n (update p.1 p.2 (oracle p.2))
          (tail.1, tail.2+1)) :=
        (measurable_fst.comp htail).prodMk (hadd.comp (measurable_snd.comp htail))
      convert (hl.sumElim hr).comp hdist using 1
      funext s
      cases h : next s <;> rw [run, h] <;>
        simp only [Function.comp_apply, h] <;> rfl

theorem measurable_simulation_joint_law_and_cost :
  ∀ {S : Type uS} {Q : Type uQ} {A : Type uA} {B : Type uB}
      {X : Type uX} {Ω : Type uΩ}
      [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace Q] [MeasurableSpace A]
      [MeasurableSpace B] [MeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSpace Ω],

        (fun x : Option X => x.elim (Sum.inl () : Unit ⊕ X) Sum.inr) inferInstance
      ∀ (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
      (next : S → Sum X Q) (update : S → Q → B → S)
      (oracle : Q → A) (target : Q → B) (decode : Q → A → B)
      (initial : Ω → S),
      Measurable next →
      Measurable (fun p : S × Q × B => update p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) →
      Measurable oracle →
      Measurable (fun p : Q × A => decode p.1 p.2) →
      Measurable initial →
      (∀ q, decode q (oracle q) = target q) →
      ∀ fuel : ℕ,

          run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel (initial ω)
        let targetRun : Ω → (S × Option X) × ℕ := fun ω =>
          run next update target fuel (initial ω)

        (∀ ω, baseRun ω = targetRun ω ∧ (baseRun ω).2 ≤ fuel) ∧
        μ.map baseRun = μ.map targetRun ∧
        IsProbabilityMeasure (μ.map baseRun) ∧
        Integrable (fun ω => ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ)) μ ∧
        (∫ ω, ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) = (∫ ω, ((targetRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) ∧
        (∫ ω, ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) ≤ (fuel : ℝ) := by

  let : MeasurableSpace (Option X) := MeasurableSpace.comap
    (fun x : Option X => x.elim (Sum.inl () : Unit ⊕ X) Sum.inr) inferInstance
  dsimp only
  intro μ hμ next update oracle target decode initial hnext hupdate horacle hdecodeMeas
    hinitial hdecode fuel
  have hsome : Measurable (@Option.some X) := by
    apply Measurable.of_comap_le
    change MeasurableSpace.comap Option.some
      (MeasurableSpace.comap
        (fun x : Option X => x.elim (Sum.inl () : Unit ⊕ X) Sum.inr) inferInstance) ≤ _
    rw [MeasurableSpace.comap_comp]
    exact (measurable_inr : Measurable (Sum.inr : X → Unit ⊕ X)).comap_le
  let baseRun : Ω → (S × Option X) × ℕ := fun ω =>
    run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle fuel (initial ω)
  let targetRun : Ω → (S × Option X) × ℕ := fun ω =>
    run next update target fuel (initial ω)
  have hcorrected : Measurable (fun p : S × Q × A =>
      update p.1 p.2.1 (decode p.2.1 p.2.2)) :=
    hupdate.comp (measurable_fst.prodMk
      (measurable_snd.fst.prodMk (hdecodeMeas.comp measurable_snd)))
  have hb : Measurable baseRun :=
    (measurable_run next (fun s q a => update s q (decode q a)) oracle
      hnext hcorrected horacle hsome fuel).comp hinitial
  have he (ω : Ω) : baseRun ω = targetRun ω ∧ (baseRun ω).2 ≤ fuel :=
    run_simulation_and_cap next update oracle target decode hdecode fuel (initial ω)
  have heq : baseRun = targetRun := funext fun ω => (he ω).1
  have ht : Measurable targetRun := by rw [← heq]; exact hb
  have hlaw : μ.map baseRun = μ.map targetRun := congrArg (fun f => μ.map f) heq
  have hprob : IsProbabilityMeasure (μ.map baseRun) :=
    Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map hb.aemeasurable
  have hcount : Measurable (fun ω => ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ)) :=
    (measurable_of_countable (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ))).comp (measurable_snd.comp hb)
  have hbound (ω : Ω) : ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ≤ (fuel : ℝ) :=
    Nat.cast_le.mpr (he ω).2
  have hint : Integrable (fun ω => ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ)) μ :=
    (integrable_const (fuel : ℝ)).mono' hcount.aestronglyMeasurable
      (ae_of_all _ fun ω => by
        rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg _)]
        exact hbound ω)
  have hcost : (∫ ω, ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) =
      (∫ ω, ((targetRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) :=
    integral_congr_ae (ae_of_all _ fun ω =>
      congrArg (fun r : (S × Option X) × ℕ => (r.2 : ℝ)) (he ω).1)
  have hmean : (∫ ω, ((baseRun ω).2 : ℝ) ∂μ) ≤ (fuel : ℝ) := by
    simpa using integral_mono hint (integrable_const (fuel : ℝ)) hbound
  exact ⟨hb, ht, he, hlaw, hprob, hint, hcost, hmean⟩
